function: Compression, quantization and feedback of downlink CSI by an autoencoder; TCQM trains with a test channel replacing the quantizer; ACLBR picks codeword length and rate (pp. 3, 5, 7).
system: Single-cell FDD massive MIMO-OFDM: BS with Nt=32 ULA antennas, single-antenna UE, 1024 subcarriers, 20 MHz; indoor 5.3 GHz (COST 2100), outdoor UMi 2.1 GHz (QuaDRiGa) (pp. 3, 7-8).
method: Autoencoders (CsiNet, CRNet) trained end to end offline on MSE reconstruction (unsupervised); Gaussian test-channel noise replaces the quantizer in training, Lloyd-Max/LBG quantizers at inference (pp. 5-8).
data_channel: Datasets generated by COST 2100 (indoor picocell, 5.3 GHz) and QuaDRiGa (outdoor UMi NLOS, 2.1 GHz, meets 3GPP 38.901); 100,000 training and 30,000 test samples, non-overlapping (pp. 7-8).
test_conditions: Non-overlapping train/test sets per scenario (indoor, outdoor), no cross-scenario test; ACLBR trains with random codeword length 10-2048; inference replaces test channel by practical quantizer (pp. 6-8, 12).
baselines: Learned CSI feedback with other quantizers on CsiNet and CRNet: retrained uniform [28], retrained LBG (KMQBlock [30]), end-to-end passing-gradient [31]; no codebook or compressive-sensing baseline (pp. 9-11).
metrics: NMSE (dB) of reconstructed CSI; validation loss and epochs to converge for ACLBR; empirical CDF check of codewords (pp. 8-13).
q1_support: p. 7: "Indoor picocellular scenario generated by COST 2100 channel model [41]"; p. 7: "generated by QuaDRiGa software [42], which meets 3GPP 38.901".
q2_support: p. 8: "The training and test datasets are non-overlapped." Indoor and outdoor are separate datasets and no model is tested on a scenario it was not trained on; swapping the test channel for practical quantizers at inference is part of the method (p. 6).
q3_support: p. 9: "let us compare the proposed TCQM with other quantization schemes for DL-based CSI feedback in the literature". All compared schemes are DL-based CSI feedback networks; no non-learned baseline such as codebook or compressive-sensing feedback (p. 1) is compared.
q4_support: p. 13: "which is approximately 1.22 for indoor scenario and 1.10 for outdoor scenario from the figure". Only the ratio of training epochs of ACLBR to a fixed (L,R) run (versus 2048 networks) is given; no order, FLOPs, parameters or runtime.
q5_support: p. 8: "The rest settings for the dataset generation are set as default in [41] and [42]." Datasets are generated by the authors with COST 2100 and QuaDRiGa; no code or data link is given.
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Area 2: CSI compression, quantization and feedback. q1 met through COST 2100 and QuaDRiGa (3GPP 38.901). q2 is 0: each scenario is trained and tested on its own disjoint split; the only train-inference mismatch is the swap of the test channel for practical quantizers, which is part of the method (p. 6, Fig. 6). q3 is 0: every baseline is a DL-based CSI feedback network with another quantizer, none is non-learned. q4 is 0: p. 7 and p. 13 analyze training cost only as an epoch-count ratio (about 1.22 indoor, 1.10 outdoor, versus 2048 networks), which is not an order, FLOPs, parameters or runtime. q5 is 0: the paper says its datasets are generated with COST 2100 and QuaDRiGa (p. 7), does not say it reuses a released dataset, and gives no link. Reviewer to confirm q2, q3 and q4.
